reasons: Hand-tuned layout numbers with no test visible.
Some lookups assume a role exists and will fail if it does not.

terms.meaning: a single point in the Atlas that can be selected
a named group of nodes of one type, such as Builds
a pseudo-random sequence that gives the same numbers every time because it starts from a fixed seed
the layout idea of a row of towers placed by year

used_by: The Atlas page and its components (not visible in this packet)

sections.name: File setup, ClusterId, NodeKind, ModelShape, Vec3
sections.title: Core types and imports
sections.what: Brings in the role, project, paper, curiosity, photo and place data, and defines the cluster, node and model names.
sections.why: The types give every node a fixed shape so the 3D scene reads them consistently.
sections.watch_out: A new node kind must be added to the kind list before it can be used.

sections.name: AtlasCluster
sections.title: Cluster shape
sections.what: Describes a cluster: an id, a short code, a label and a description.
sections.why: Gives each group of nodes a visible name.

sections.name: AtlasLink
sections.title: Outside link shape
sections.what: Describes a labelled web link attached to a node.
sections.why: Lets nodes point to papers or live demos.

sections.name: AtlasNode
sections.title: Node shape
sections.what: Lists every field a node may hold: identity, cluster, text, links, shape, photo, size, year, scene details and 3D position.
sections.why: One shape keeps all node types in one list.
sections.watch_out: Every node needs a position, or it cannot be placed.

sections.name: SceneInfo
sections.title: Project scene details
sections.what: Holds a project's number in its role, its industry, its problem type and its locations, shown beside its scene.
sections.why: Lets the gallery show project details without re-reading the data.

sections.name: AtlasEdge
sections.title: Relationship shape
sections.what: A link has a start, an end and a kind such as contains, built, sector, informs, context or illustrative.
sections.why: The kind decides what the relationship means on screen.
sections.watch_out: A kind outside the allowed list fails the type check.

sections.name: clusters
sections.title: The seven clusters
sections.what: Defines the seven clusters in order, with codes S01 to S07, names and descriptions.
sections.why: Keeps the visible cluster names and descriptions together.

sections.name: rng, round
sections.title: Repeatable random numbers and rounding
sections.what: Creates a seeded random generator so the same seed gives the same numbers, and rounds values to two decimal places.
sections.why: Keeps positions stable so coordinates do not shuffle between builds.
sections.watch_out: Changing a seed or the number of random calls moves every node that uses them.

sections.name: yearsOf
sections.title: Years of a role
sections.what: Reads the years from a role's period text; a period marked present runs to 2026.5.
sections.why: Years set each tower's width and its place on the timeline.
sections.watch_out: Needs a four-digit year in the text; without one the year is undefined.

sections.name: timeline
sections.title: Roles in time order
sections.what: Sorts roles by start year and sets the timeline from 2012.5 to 2027.5 across a street 96 units long.
sections.why: Keeps the street in time order.
sections.watch_out: Changing the timeline limits shifts every tower sideways.

sections.name: xForYear
sections.title: Year to street position
sections.what: Converts a year into a horizontal position along the street, centred on zero.
sections.why: Puts each item at the right point in time. The half-width of the street is also set here.

sections.name: towerSide, Draft, drafts
sections.title: Tower sides and draft list
sections.what: Alternates towers between the two sides of the street, and creates the empty list that collects nodes before final codes are given.
sections.why: Alternating sides keeps neighbouring towers from overlapping.
sections.watch_out: Drafts have no code yet; do not read codes from them.

sections.name: towerPos
sections.title: Towers and engagement floors
sections.what: For each role in time order, sets the tower's size and position from its years and project count, then adds the role node and one node per engagement, stacked as floors.
sections.why: Taller and wider towers show roles with more projects and more years.
sections.watch_out: Heights divide by the project count; this is safe only because the loop does not run when the count is zero.

sections.name: ORIGIN_EXP
sections.title: Origins for builds
sections.what: Maps two origin keys to the roles they belong to; any other origin counts as independent.
sections.why: Lets builds sit beside the role they came from.
sections.watch_out: Only two origins are listed, so a new origin falls back to the independent group.

sections.name: buildGroups
sections.title: Builds beside their roles
sections.what: Groups projects by origin and places each in a row beside its role's tower, or at the present end of the street for independent builds, with links to its page and code.
sections.why: Keeps builds near their source role so the story reads along the street.
sections.watch_out: Independent builds all gather near the present end, so new independent builds crowd that spot.

sections.name: industryRoles
sections.title: Industry nodes above roles
sections.what: Creates one node per industry, placed above the average position of its roles, taller when more roles share it.
sections.why: Shows where each sector sits relative to the work.
sections.watch_out: Industry names come from the role data; a typo creates a separate industry node.

sections.name: SceneDraft
sections.title: Project scene shape
sections.what: Describes a scene draft: the scene details plus the role id and description.
sections.why: Keeps scenes typed before they are placed.

sections.name: scenesByRole, sceneCount, momentCount
sections.title: Scenes and counts per role
sections.what: Makes one scene per key project for each role, or one general scene if it has none, and counts the scenes and photo moments for each role.
sections.why: Each role gets the same sequence in its gallery.
sections.watch_out: These counts decide the gallery height, so adding a photo changes the layout.

sections.name: momentHub, anchors
sections.title: Gallery hub above each role
sections.what: Works out the centre point of a role's gallery, raised as its rows increase, and sets up storage for gallery anchors.
sections.why: The hub is the point the view aims at.
sections.watch_out: Assumes the role exists in the tower list; an unknown role will crash this step.

sections.name: galleryPos, momentAnchor, galleryCenter
sections.title: Gallery positions and anchors
sections.what: Places each scene or photo on a grid of four columns behind its role, records the direction each faces, and exposes lookups for anchors and gallery centres.
sections.why: Rooms face outward so visitors look away from the street.
sections.watch_out: The grid is fixed at four columns; changing it moves every gallery.

sections.name: galleryRows
sections.title: Scenes and papers into galleries
sections.what: Adds one gallery node per project scene, each with a spec sheet of role, project number, problem, location and period, then places the research papers in the research gallery.
sections.why: The spec sheets are drawn in 3D from these rows.
sections.watch_out: Papers are placed in the research role's gallery by a fixed role id, so new papers always join that gallery.

sections.name: ideaDrafts
sections.title: Research threads and curiosities as pavilions
sections.what: Makes an idea node for each open research thread and each curiosity, then spreads them in a ring of pavilions beyond the end of the street.
sections.why: Ideas are not tied to a year, so they sit off the timeline.
sections.watch_out: The ring is spread evenly, so the more ideas there are, the tighter the spacing.

sections.name: visualBase, paperMemoryIds
sections.title: Visual archive and paper memory ids
sections.what: Places the portrait and three placeholder 3D shapes in the visual archive, and builds a set of ids for papers so photos already shown as papers are not duplicated.
sections.why: The ids let the photo step skip papers that already have nodes.
sections.watch_out: The three shapes are placeholders, not real models.

sections.name: memByRole, extraNodes
sections.title: Photos into role galleries
sections.what: Places each non-paper photo in its role's gallery as a numbered moment, and creates an empty list for extra hand-added nodes.
sections.why: Photos sit beside the role they belong to.
sections.watch_out: Photos whose role is missing from the timeline are skipped silently, so a typo in a role id removes them.

sections.name: nodes, ids
sections.title: Final node list and codes
sections.what: Combines all the nodes and gives each one a code such as N-001, and records the set of ids for link checks.
sections.why: Codes give visitors a short reference on screen.
sections.watch_out: Codes come from position, so adding or moving a node earlier renumbers the later ones.

sections.name: derived
sections.title: Automatic links for roles
sections.what: Starts the link list with contains links from roles to their engagements, papers and photos, built links to their builds, and sector links to their industries.
sections.why: Relationships come from the data, so the graph updates when the data changes.

sections.name: industryNames
sections.title: Engagements linked to industries
sections.what: Connects each engagement to an industry node when the names match, so it appears under the right sector.
sections.why: Likely reason: matching names avoids a separate mapping list.
sections.watch_out: Matching is loose: it uses partial names and first words, so unrelated industries can be linked by accident.

sections.name: b, extraEdges, edges
sections.title: Hand-written links and final edges
sections.what: Adds named relationships between ideas, curiosities, builds, papers and visual shapes, then returns only links whose two ends exist.
sections.why: Some relationships cannot be worked out from the data, so they are written by hand.
sections.watch_out: A typo in a hand-written id drops that link silently.

sections.name: neighbours, clusterOf
sections.title: Neighbours and cluster lookup
sections.what: Returns every node linked to a given node, and finds a cluster's details by its id.
sections.why: Used to show related items beside a selected node.
sections.watch_out: The cluster lookup assumes the id exists and fails for an unknown one.

sections.name: overviewOf
sections.title: Summary of one role
sections.what: Groups everything attached to one role (engagements, builds, industries, papers and photos) for its overview panel. The file also exports the tower positions.
sections.why: Likely reason: the overview panel needs these lists split by type.
sections.watch_out: Assumes the role exists in the battle list; an unknown id causes an error.

summary: Builds the 3D Atlas graph: every role, engagement, build, industry, paper, photo and idea, placed in space and linked to related items.
purpose: Supplies the Atlas with its points, their positions, their text and the links between them.
why: The header comment says roles stand in time order along a street, so positions match real time, and placement is fixed so the coordinates shown are the true ones.
how: 1) Defines the shapes for clusters, nodes and links. 2) Places each role as a tower along the timeline. 3) Stacks engagements as floors inside each tower, puts builds beside their origin role, and puts industries above their roles. 4) Places each role's project scenes and photos in a wall of rooms, with papers and idea pavilions. 5) Gives each node a code such as N-001. 6) Creates the links, then keeps only links whose two ends exist.
inputs: Battle (role) data, project data, research papers and threads, curiosities, the photo and portrait registry, and place data.
outputs: The node list, the edge list, the cluster list, the timeline and helper lookups used by the Atlas.
risks: Positions come from hand-tuned numbers, so changing a role's years moves its tower and everything attached. Codes depend on order, so adding a node renumbers later ones. Some lookups assume a role exists and fail if it does not. Links to missing nodes are dropped silently.
debug: If a node is missing, check it was added to the node list and that its owner matches a role id. If links are missing, check both ends exist with exact ids. If a tower is misplaced, check its period text includes years. Changed codes after an edit are expected.
